To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the same children remained poor readers year after years, (2) the same children did not remain poor writers year to year, (3) the poor readers had little phonemic awareness in first grade, (4) the poor readers did not achieve the level of decoding skills that the good readers achieved by the beginning of second grades, (5) the poor readers read considerably less than the good readers both in and outside of school, and (6) the Simple View of Reading and
the Simple View of Reading and Writing (Gough, Juel, & Griffith, 1996) is a useful framework for understanding literacy acquisition and development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of reading and writing in children from first through fifth grade.
literacy acquisition in children from first through sixth grade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the children in this study who remained poor readers were those who lacked phonemic awareness at the beginning of first grade and were not taught decoding skills in first grade.
poor readers are not poor readers because they do not read, but rather poor readers do not read because they are poor readers.

the poor readers and poor writers in this study were not able to acquire literacy in a timely manner because of a lack of phonemic awareness, a lack of reading experience, and a lack of writing experience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simple view of reading and writing is an accurate model for the development of reading and writing in children.
the children who became poor readers in first grade had not achieved the level or phonemic awareness that the good readers achieved at the beginning second grade.
children who were not able to read by the end of first or second grade were not likely to become good readers by the end of fourth or fifth grade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same children remain at the same levels of performance in reading and writing year after year.
the same children remain the same readers year after year.
the same children remain the poor readers and writers year after year.
